doc.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

title: Playing a club at 15 to support the family
summary: After his father's death Tiberi worked in a club at 15 earning 30 dollars a week, and joined Bob Chester's orchestra in 1948.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yes. Let me take you back. I’m interested in the very start of your musical career. And I believe I read that taking up music was partly a practical thing, a family decision. You were helping make money for the family. Is that correct?

Well at 15 — my father died after an accident actually — when I was 12, and at 15 I was in a club. And ironically I was singing “Caledonia” and playing the “Woodchopper’s Ball” you know with a small group with a trumpet and sax. And I was making 30 dollars a week and that was supporting the family. I mean right now it’s about five thousand a week.
And you were playing the saxophone?
So I was looking at — this would have been let’s say 1947 or so?
Let’s see. Maybe — I’ve got some notes over here. That would be — well ’48 — well it would be that time actually. In ’48 I joined Bob Chester’s orchestra.
